source: Reply from an author of Iwasaki et al., AAPS J 2020;22:66, to the platform owner (personal communication, 30 October 2026). Kept by the platform owner only; not committed (private correspondence).

answers.question: How should the equations provided on request be credited?
answers.consequence: The model is credited as Iwasaki et al., AAPS J 2020;22:66 (doi:10.1208/s12248-020-00448-x). The extract's note that attribution wording is pending is resolved; no individual is named as the source of the equations.

answers.question: How does an intravenous dose enter the model?
answers.answer: As a bolus into the central compartment.
answers.consequence: Confirms the dose-input assumption of the locked 3.0k check (IV bolus into systemic plasma, Cp). Initial conditions (all compartments at zero before the first dose) were not asked; they remain the plan's standard reading. The 3.0k result (not consistent with Ogawa 2008 or CAN-1004, robust) no longer rests on an assumed dose input. The locked plan and report are unchanged.

still_open: Which human data were used to evaluate the model (independence of Ogawa 2008 and CAN-1004 for the 3.0k comparison).
The pharmacodynamic equation for blood proteasome inhibition (not needed for the PK check).
